title: Coherence of Seifert circles and the height of a diagram
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $C,C'$ be two disjoint oriented circles in $S^2$ and let $A$ be the annulus they cobound. Orient $A$; the orientation induces a boundary orientation on each of $C$ and $C'$ (the boundary components of an oriented annulus receive opposite induced orientations). Say that $C$ and $C'$ are **coherent** when the two given orientations induce, relative to some (equivalently, any) orientation of $A$, opposite signs of agreement with the induced boundary orientations; equivalently, when $C$ and $C'$ represent the same element of $H_1(A;\mathbb Z)$ under their given orientations. For an oriented diagram $D$, the **height** $h(D)$ is the number of distinct unordered pairs of incoherent Seifert circles of $D$. In the published conventions of the sources, $h(D)=0$ means that all pairs of Seifert circles are coherent.
strategy: The sign formulation is well defined because reversing the orientation of $A$ flips both induced boundary orientations; the homology formulation identifies the same relation and is the version stated in the survey. Coherence is defined for every pair of Seifert circles, not only adjacent ones. AC is consumed exactly through the annulus lemma, which supplies the three-component structure of the complement of two disjoint circles (Jordan-Brouwer separation and Schoenflies); no other step of the definition uses choice.
